title: Backpressure & Power-aware Kernel Trace Collector for Per-Stream Profiling
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add a low-overhead collector that correlates scheduler backpressure signals, per-kernel NVTX spans, and GPU power/SM utilization samples to produce per-stream energy and latency attribution. Output will drive console SLO dashboards, runtime batching heuristics, and a new 'backpressure score' metric exposed on request-level traces. This ticket covers design + prototype + rollout for host-side sampling (DCGM/rapl), lightweight driver hooks for kernel tagging, trace enrichment pipeline, and dashboard templates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Collector can join NVTX ranges and runtime trace spans into a coherent per-request timeline with >=95% correlation fidelity on synthetic workloads. 2) End-to-end pipeline adds <1.5% latency overhead and <3% p99 CPU overhead on control-plane nodes under representative load. 3) Grafana dashboard shows per-model per-route energy-per-token and backpressure score; alert rule for sudden backpressure regressions. 4) Documented rollout plan and opt-out for Dedicated/Private customers.
tasks: Design sampling cadence and counter set (SM util, mem bw, power, kernel occupancy)
Implement host-side sampler connector using DCGM + procfs as fallback
Instrument runtime to emit consistent NVTX envelope IDs for prefill/decode kernels
Enrich trace spans in collector to attach energy buckets and backpressure score
Ship initial Grafana dashboard and alert rules
Run load test on staging with 1000 concurrent streams and validate overhead
risks_and_mitigation: Sampling overhead: keep cadence adaptive; fall back to event-driven samples when load low
Signal fidelity: add synthetic workload fuzzers to assert correlation; store hashed span anchors, not PII
Storage cost: roll up per-request raw samples to 1s aggregates and retain detailed traces only for flagged anomalies
Customer privacy: provide opt-out and ensure no customer payloads are persisted by collector
comments: 2026-03-05 Maya Chen: Drafted initial problem statement after customer call (RetailAI): they reported tail latency spikes that correlate with model switches. Proposed combining NVTX + DCGM samples to find energy/latency hotspots.
2026-03-07 Luca Romero: Spike prototype landed that emits a 64-bit envelope id on NVTX begin/end and streams to /dev/shm. Initial microbench shows ~0.6% CPU overhead at 1000 qps.
2026-03-09 Design review (Ivan Petrov): Recommended adaptive sampling and a coarse-grained aggregation to control storage. Also asked for a privacy checklist for Private deployments.
2026-03-10 QA: Found sporadic loss of envelope IDs when kernel preemption occurs; investigating ordering guarantees and adding sequence numbers to spans.
2026-03-11 Security (Asha Reddy): Flagged KMS usage for persisting any sampled payloads; requested opt-out and encryption-at-rest for staging artifacts.
2026-03-12 Performance (Ravi Kapoor): Load testing on staging-3 showed p99 CPU overhead ~1.1% and added 8% IO for metrics export at 5000 concurrent streams; next: test with aggregation window tuning.

2026-03-13 Luca Romero: Merged collector prototype behind feature flag; open PR for dashboards and playbook. Next steps: run a week-long soak with synthetic mixes and schedule rollout to one internal team.
